 Darius Acuff Jr. gets honest about Kings veterans, criticism over shot attempts 
 2026-11-04 20:33 
 Sacramento Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. addressed rumors of tension with team's veterans, insisting that team chemistry remains strong. He also dismissed criticism of his high shot attempts, emphasizing his focus on improving and helping the team.
 Credit: Getty Images via AFP - Scanpix 
 Credit Getty Images via AFP - Scanpix 
 Credit Getty Images via AFP - Scanpix

 Sacramento Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. has addressed recent rumors surrounding his relationship with team's veterans, as well as the growing attention surrounding his shot attempts.

 Recent reports suggested that Kings star Domantas Sabonis has been "not enthused" about playing alongside the rookie.
 However, Acuff dismissed the speculation, insisting that his relationship with everyone on the team has been great so far.
 "It's great, man. They're there for me every game, every practice, every day. You know, every single play in the game, they give me advice, good or bad, just letting me know when certain things are there," Acuff told reporters on Wednesday.
 "Everybody on the team, vets, second-year players, whatever, we all just got great chemistry and great trust. So it's great."
 When asked whether the rumors have affected him in any way, the rookie made it clear that his only focus is playing basketball and helping his team.
 "Not at all. I just go out and hoop for my team," he stated.
 Darius Acuff Jr. responds to criticism over shot attempts
 Through the first seven games of his NBA career, Acuff has attempted 165 field goals, leading the league with an average of 23.6 shot attempts per game.
 His high shooting volume has attracted considerable attention, but the rookie insisted that he is not concerned about what the media has been saying.
 "Not a lot. I mean, I'm just trying to keep getting better every game, not worrying about what the media is saying or that. I'm just out here hooping and trying to get better for my team, build chemistry with them every game. So it's going good," Acuff explained.
 When asked about the freedom he has been given to play his game, take shots, and log significant minutes as a rookie, Acuff emphasized the trust he has received from his coaches and teammates.
 "I don't think it's about that. I think that's just how I affect the game, how I play, how I've always played. And I got a coaching staff who believe in me. I got teammates who believe in me. We all believe in each other. So I think when you build that trust and chemistry, it all goes along."
